items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: So Lee Bouveau got another place for me to live that he had to pay for.

ctx.x: I don't get to realize nothing. Take it the way it goes. The film company wanted to get a signature from the agent that told them about me and they paid the one-way ticket to be sure I would be there. Send me a round-trip ticket? No, that was too much to do. They send me a one-way ticket, it's easy

to get the ticket going back if I'm going to work for them. But they sent the one-way ticket. I don't know. They tell me they're going to give me a thousand dollars a week and all expenses paid, so I'm beginning to wonder - I don't got but the one-way ticket, 'cause I had to pay my own fare out of the thousand dollars. I'm not worried about not paying me. I'm just worried about getting over there, that's all. But I didn't know there wasn't going to be no job. That's the way it was. I didn't know there wasn't…
agency paid for it because they okayed me to leave there to go to Kaiserslautern.
